unsupported operator: except: The two-list except function has no list-difference lowering in this translator.
unsupported operator: matches: Regex matches() has no lowering: CEL uses RE2 and SQL regex dialects do not preserve its matching/error semantics, including through boolean equality.
unsupported operator: index: Ordered list indexing has no SQL relation lowering; a relation has no positional order or CEL out-of-bounds/error semantics.
Positional access into a scalar list. tagNames is a related table and row order in a SQL relation is not defined, so `index` has no case in the vendored translator

Positional access into a list of numbers or booleans. `index` has no case in the vendored translator, so the walk refuses the operator itself, before any mapping is resolved or the element's JSON type can matter: a list stored as a related table has no defined row order to read position 0 from, and the mapper has no ordered array or JSON column kind to lower it against instead
'int()' cannot be lowered to SQL CAST: Negated int() remains unsupported: SQL CAST accepts numeric prefixes where CEL requires the whole string and errors otherwise; negation must not turn those errors into matches.
timestamp() over a column requires that: timestamp() cannot lower an arbitrary string column: malformed strings must remain CEL evaluation errors under negation; only a typed timestamp column or valid literal is supported.
'double()' cannot be lowered to SQL CAST: Negated double() remains unsupported: SQL CAST accepts numeric prefixes where CEL requires the whole string and errors otherwise; negation must not turn those errors into matches.
unsupported operator: matches. CEL's reg: The translator has no matches lowering: the SQL engines do not share CEL RE2 semantics.
'exists' requires a collection attribute: The planner emits list/struct/set-field constructors for principal objects; the macro fold accepts literal value lists or mapped relations, not constructor expressions.
exists_one over a literal collection val: This macro has no value-list lowering; only exists/all can use the translator’s literal-list fold.
'filter' requires a collection attribute: This macro has no value-list lowering; only exists/all can use the translator’s literal-list fold.
'map' requires a collection attribute: This macro has no value-list lowering; only exists/all can use the translator’s literal-list fold.
unsupported operator: list: The computed list constructor has no SQL scalar lowering in this translator.

The descendant path is CONSTRUCTED by list() from a constant segment and the primary key rather than read from a column. `list` has never reached the wire from this corpus, so the translator has no case for it and the walk fails closed before the hierarchy operators around it are reached
conditional value used where a plain exp: The divisor resolves to a conditional IEEE value; division requires a plain SQL expression and cannot bind the symbolic branches.
bare temporal attributes compare RFC 333: Native timestamp storage discards the original RFC 3339 spelling, so instant equality cannot reproduce CEL string equality without timestamp() wrappers.
attribute \"request.resource.attr.tagNam: The mapped relation stores individual members, and cannot be resolved as one scalar comparison operand for whole-list equality.
unsupported operator: struct: A struct constructor is not a scalar SQL operand and has no lowering in this translator.
membership with a list-valued element ca: A nested list element cannot be bound as a scalar member of this relation.
hasIntersection between two stored colle: The computed list constructor has no SQL scalar lowering in this translator.
'int()' cannot be lowered to SQL CAST: C: int() is required to give `%` an integer operand and has no faithful SQL lowering, so the cast fails closed before the modulo is reached — the same refusal as cast-int-double
'map' produces a collection rather than: map() is held as a deferred collection until size() or hasIntersection() gives it a scalar meaning. Comparing the ordered projection itself to a literal list gives it none, so the held collection reaches a plain value position and is refused there
hierarchy() delimiter must be a non-empt: The vendored translator rejects an empty hierarchy delimiter before any operator is lowered: a path cannot be split into segments on an empty string, and the descendant test is emitted as `prefix || delimiter || '%'`, which with an empty delimiter would match the path itself (a2, never its own descendant) and every string extension of it
